title: Hpakant jade-mining district: observed surface change

story.headline: Real NISAR radar over the world's largest jade-mining district
story.context: Hpakant's open-pit jade mines are hard to inspect on the ground and cloud hides them through the monsoon. These are real NISAR L-band passes from 2026-05-01 to 2026-10-16. Between the baseline and the latest pass, 5 ha of formerly vegetated ground lost more than 3 dB of radar return, confirmed on two consecutive passes, and 6 ha became open water.
story.radar_insight: Vegetation scatters L-band radar many times (volume scattering), which keeps the cross-polarised (HV) return bright. Stripped, dug or dumped ground returns far less HV, and calm water reflects radar away, so it shows dark in HH too. InSAR coherence adds a clue: ground disturbed between two passes decorrelates.

uncertainty.null_test: Same rule between the two baseline passes (2026-05-01 and 2026-05-25), where little real change is expected.
notes: Moisture changes between the dry-season baseline and the monsoon passes can lower or raise backscatter locally; the per-pass offset removes only scene-wide shifts.
Steep terrain causes layover and shadow; a change on a steep slope may be a landslide or mine-waste slide rather than excavation.
Provisional NISAR products: calibration may change when ASF reprocesses them.
Minimum mapping unit 1 ha; smaller workings are missed.
Not yet validated against field data or optical imagery.
